```json
{
  "technical_and_design_decisions": [
    "The software increment will be developed as an extension module for an existing Spring-based backend system, likely a data processing platform (e.g., Stream processing, CF/Cloud Foundry related). We will assume an existing architecture with Spring Boot, possibly using Spring Cloud for configuration.",
    "We will implement the RxJava module (U1) using RxJava 3 and create a Spring-compatible processor/transformer interface. The design will follow an adapter pattern to integrate RxJava streams with the existing data processing pipeline.",
    "For ACL (U2), a research and design spike is required. The initial implementation will be a minimal prototype (e.g., a new annotation `@RequiresPermission` and a basic `PermissionService`) to validate the approach. The full DSL/UI scope will be deferred as per the spike description.",
    "HDFS storage for uber-jars (U4/U5/U6) will be implemented using Hadoop's `FileSystem` API. The location will be configurable via Spring properties, defaulting to a known HDFS path. We will handle upload, download, and checksum verification for reliability.",
    "YARN config location override (U7) will be implemented by allowing the user to specify a custom YARN configuration file path (e.g., `yarn-site.xml`) via a Spring property, which the client will use to initialize the YARN `Configuration` object.",
    "For stopping Spark jobs (U8), we will integrate with Spark's `SparkContext.stop()` or use the Spark REST API/YARN application manager to trigger job termination, depending on the cluster deployment mode.",
    "Performance investigation (U3) is a research spike, not implementation. It will involve profiling tooling (e.g., VisualVM, async-profiler), creating test harnesses, and documenting findings.",
    "We will use Spring Boot's configuration properties (`@ConfigurationProperties`) for all new configurable locations and options (for U4-U7) to maintain consistency and ease of use.",
    "Assume the project uses a standard CI/CD pipeline, and the development follows an Agile process with 1-2 week sprints. Unit tests (JUnit 5, Mockito) and integration tests (Testcontainers for HDFS/Hadoop) will be required for implemented features."
  ],
  "assumptions": [
    "The developer (myself) is fully skilled in Java, Spring, RxJava, Hadoop/HDFS, YARN, and Spark APIs. No learning time is factored into the estimates.",
    "The existing system has an established codebase, build system (Maven/Gradle), and testing framework. Initial project setup and dependency management are already in place.",
    "The 'user stories' are for a single software increment to be delivered in one development cycle. U4 and U5 are identical and are treated as a single requirement.",
    "For U2 (ACL), the scope is limited to the *Spike Scope*: design research, API specification, and a minimal proof-of-concept. No production-ready UI or comprehensive DSL is included.",
    "For U3 (Performance Investigation), the scope is analysis only. No code changes to optimize the system are included in this estimate; only profiling, identification, and documentation.",
    "Effort estimates include analysis, coding, unit testing, and basic integration testing for each activity. They do not include deployment, long-term monitoring, or extensive QA cycles.",
    "The software increment is built on top of a framework similar to Spring Cloud Data Flow (SCDF) or a custom stream processing platform, given the context of 'processor', 'CF user', 'uber-jar', 'Spark job', etc.",
    "For HDFS/YARN operations (U4, U5, U6, U7), we assume network connectivity and necessary client libraries (Hadoop client) are already available in the project's dependency scope."
  ],
  "activities": [
    {
      "activity_id": "A1",
      "activity_name": "Architecture Design & Project Scaffolding",
      "activity_description": "Define the overall module structure for the increment. Create necessary packages, base classes, and Spring Boot auto-configuration skeletons. Document the integration points with the existing system for the new features (RxJava, ACL, HDFS, YARN, Spark).",
      "most_likely_effort": 20
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A2",
      "activity_name": "Implement Flexible RxJava Module (U1)",
      "activity_description": "Develop the RxJava integration module. Create an interface for defining processors using RxJava 2/3 `Flowable`/`Observable`. Implement adapters to connect RxJava streams with the existing platform's internal data model/event system. Write unit tests for the core operators and adapters.",
      "most_likely_effort": 32
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A3",
      "activity_name": "ACL Design & Prototype Implementation (U2)",
      "activity_description": "Conduct research spike: Review customer use cases, design ACL data model (users, roles, resources, permissions), and define key APIs. Implement a minimal prototype: a `@RequiresPermission` method annotation, a basic `PermissionEvaluator` aspect, and a simple in-memory ACL repository. Document design specs, scope for future DSL/UI, and next steps.",
      "most_likely_effort": 40
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A4",
      "activity_name": "HDFS Storage & Config Override for Modules (U4, U5, U6, U7)",
      "activity_description": "Implement functionality to store and retrieve a custom module uber-jar in HDFS. Create a `HdfsModuleRepository` class with methods for `upload`, `download`, `getUri`. Implement configurable HDFS base path via Spring property (`app.module.hdfs.base-path`). Implement functionality to override the YARN client configuration location via Spring property (`app.yarn.config-path`). Write unit tests with a mock HDFS file system and integration tests using MiniDfsCluster or Testcontainers.",
      "most_likely_effort": 24
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A5",
      "activity_name": "Spark Job Stop Functionality (U8)",
      "activity_description": "Implement a service to stop a running Spark job. Create a `SparkJobManager` with a method `stopJob(String applicationId)`. Determine the correct stop mechanism (e.g., `SparkContext.stop()` if context is available, YARN client `killApplication`, or Spark REST API call). Handle error cases and return meaningful status. Write unit and integration tests.",
      "most_likely_effort": 16
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A6",
      "activity_name": "Performance Investigation Analysis (U3)",
      "activity_description": "Conduct performance spike: Set up profiling environment. Perform CPU profiling on both 'admin' and 'container' servers during startup. Identify bottlenecks using profiling data. Document findings, root causes, and list pros/cons of potential optimization approaches. Create a profiling report and a short presentation for the team.",
      "most_likely_effort": 20
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A7",
      "activity_name": "Integration Testing & Documentation",
      "activity_description": "Write integration tests for the entire increment (e.g., test a flow using the RxJava processor, test module deployment from HDFS, test job stop). Update or create module-level documentation, including configuration properties, usage examples for the new RxJava processor, and notes on the ACL prototype. Prepare demo-ready code snippets.",
      "most_likely_effort": 24
    }
  ],
  "reported_total": {
    "most_likely_effort": 176
  }
}
```

technical_and_design_decisions: The software increment will be developed as an extension module for an existing Spring-based backend system, likely a data processing platform (e.g., Stream processing, CF/Cloud Foundry related). We will assume an existing architecture with Spring Boot, possibly using Spring Cloud for configuration.

We will implement the RxJava module (U1) using RxJava 3 and create a Spring-compatible processor/transformer interface. The design will follow an adapter pattern to integrate RxJava streams with the existing data processing pipeline.

For ACL (U2), a research and design spike is required. The initial implementation will be a minimal prototype (e.g., a new annotation `@RequiresPermission` and a basic `PermissionService`) to validate the approach. The full DSL/UI scope will be deferred as per the spike description.

HDFS storage for uber-jars (U4/U5/U6) will be implemented using Hadoop's `FileSystem` API. The location will be configurable via Spring properties, defaulting to a known HDFS path. We will handle upload, download, and checksum verification for reliability.

YARN config location override (U7) will be implemented by allowing the user to specify a custom YARN configuration file path (e.g., `yarn-site.xml`) via a Spring property, which the client will use to initialize the YARN `Configuration` object.

For stopping Spark jobs (U8), we will integrate with Spark's `SparkContext.stop()` or use the Spark REST API/YARN application manager to trigger job termination, depending on the cluster deployment mode.
Performance investigation (U3) is a research spike, not implementation. It will involve profiling tooling (e.g., VisualVM, async-profiler), creating test harnesses, and documenting findings.
We will use Spring Boot's configuration properties (`@ConfigurationProperties`) for all new configurable locations and options (for U4-U7) to maintain consistency and ease of use.

Assume the project uses a standard CI/CD pipeline, and the development follows an Agile process with 1-2 week sprints. Unit tests (JUnit 5, Mockito) and integration tests (Testcontainers for HDFS/Hadoop) will be required for implemented features.
assumptions: The developer (myself) is fully skilled in Java, Spring, RxJava, Hadoop/HDFS, YARN, and Spark APIs. No learning time is factored into the estimates.
The existing system has an established codebase, build system (Maven/Gradle), and testing framework. Initial project setup and dependency management are already in place.
The 'user stories' are for a single software increment to be delivered in one development cycle. U4 and U5 are identical and are treated as a single requirement.
For U2 (ACL), the scope is limited to the *Spike Scope*: design research, API specification, and a minimal proof-of-concept. No production-ready UI or comprehensive DSL is included.
For U3 (Performance Investigation), the scope is analysis only. No code changes to optimize the system are included in this estimate; only profiling, identification, and documentation.
Effort estimates include analysis, coding, unit testing, and basic integration testing for each activity. They do not include deployment, long-term monitoring, or extensive QA cycles.

The software increment is built on top of a framework similar to Spring Cloud Data Flow (SCDF) or a custom stream processing platform, given the context of 'processor', 'CF user', 'uber-jar', 'Spark job', etc.
For HDFS/YARN operations (U4, U5, U6, U7), we assume network connectivity and necessary client libraries (Hadoop client) are already available in the project's dependency scope.

activities.activity_description: Define the overall module structure for the increment. Create necessary packages, base classes, and Spring Boot auto-configuration skeletons. Document the integration points with the existing system for the new features (RxJava, ACL, HDFS, YARN, Spark).

Develop the RxJava integration module. Create an interface for defining processors using RxJava 2/3 `Flowable`/`Observable`. Implement adapters to connect RxJava streams with the existing platform's internal data model/event system. Write unit tests for the core operators and adapters.

Conduct research spike: Review customer use cases, design ACL data model (users, roles, resources, permissions), and define key APIs. Implement a minimal prototype: a `@RequiresPermission` method annotation, a basic `PermissionEvaluator` aspect, and a simple in-memory ACL repository. Document design specs, scope for future DSL/UI, and next steps.

activities.activity_name: HDFS Storage & Config Override for Modules (U4, U5, U6, U7)
activities.activity_description: Implement functionality to store and retrieve a custom module uber-jar in HDFS. Create a `HdfsModuleRepository` class with methods for `upload`, `download`, `getUri`. Implement configurable HDFS base path via Spring property (`app.module.hdfs.base-path`). Implement functionality to override the YARN client configuration location via Spring property (`app.yarn.config-path`). Write unit tests with a mock HDFS file system and integration tests using MiniDfsCluster or Testcontainers.

Implement a service to stop a running Spark job. Create a `SparkJobManager` with a method `stopJob(String applicationId)`. Determine the correct stop mechanism (e.g., `SparkContext.stop()` if context is available, YARN client `killApplication`, or Spark REST API call). Handle error cases and return meaningful status. Write unit and integration tests.

Conduct performance spike: Set up profiling environment. Perform CPU profiling on both 'admin' and 'container' servers during startup. Identify bottlenecks using profiling data. Document findings, root causes, and list pros/cons of potential optimization approaches. Create a profiling report and a short presentation for the team.

Write integration tests for the entire increment (e.g., test a flow using the RxJava processor, test module deployment from HDFS, test job stop). Update or create module-level documentation, including configuration properties, usage examples for the new RxJava processor, and notes on the ACL prototype. Prepare demo-ready code snippets.
